{"sourceType":"ESA Tender Action","sourceSystem":"ESA esa-star Publication","sourcePage":"https://esastar-publication-ext.sso.esa.int/ESATenderActions/filter/open","id":182226,"idEra":24590,"activityNumber":"1000045580","contractNumber":"","tanumber":"1-13263","title":"T711-901SD DYNAMIC LOCATION AND TIME-WINDOW UNCERTAINTIES DURING UNCONTROLLED RE-ENTRY (EXPRO+)","description":"Historical data associated with the uncontrolled re-entry of satellite and rocket bodies yielded that, as a rule of thumb, the driving uncertainty of where these events take place can be linked to 20% of the remaining orbital lifetime and that there is an underlying 50% uncertainty on the drag experienced between 80 and 200 km. These uncertainties are mostly empirical and neglect any relationwith the actual object shape and resulting drag, and feature as input to design for demise envelope condition when it comes to establishing fragmentation altitude and as such influence casualty risk reduction developments.
